newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Schering Q1 97 profits rise 10-15 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Schering Q1 97 profits rise 10-15 pct.

text.p: German pharmaceutical group Schering AG said on Wednesday that its profits for the first quarter of 1997 had risen between 10 and 15 percent from a year earlier, while group sales were up 21 percent.
The firm also said that the current dollar/mark exchange rate would boost profits for the year as whole by around 10 to 15 percent.
Schering's board chairman Giuseppe Vita told the firm's annual meeting that the first three months of this year had developed very favourably due to the dollar/mark level.
The mark has weakened substantially against the dollar in recent months and was trading at 1.7275 in mid-morning trade on Wednesday.
In 1996, Schering said its total sales were 5.27 billion marks -- a figure which Vita said would this year rise by 14 percent to around six billion marks.
Schering also said it planned to buy back large amounts of its own shares when this became legally possible.
A spokesman said the company would buy back shares in several chunks, but added that Schering did not see itself at risk of a hostile takeover attempt as it was "too expensive and too specialised."
The spokesman said Schering had a current market value of 11 billion marks and that a potential buyer would have to offer at least 16 billion marks.
Moreover, the company's structure was so streamlined that "not even 5,000 people could be let go" after a takeover.
The German share market reacted positively to the figures and news of the share buy-back.
Sharing's stock gained 4.80 marks, around three percent, to 165.80 in bourse trade, while the overall market was up 55.73 points, or 1.65 percent, at 3,438.92 points.
"It seems to have triggered speculative buys," said Andreas Schmidt, chemicals analyst at BZW Deutschland, who has a 'buy' recommendation on Schering.
"The numbers themselves were nothing special, in fact just slightly below our expectations, but the share had also underperformed in the past few days and is catching up now," he added.
